display.purpose: The reset countdown, and nothing else. Tabular, italic, 800. Seconds ride as a dim small at ~38% of parent size.

headline.purpose: The single page headline. It sits below the stage, never above the bar.

title.purpose: HUD plates: gauge names, product name, fact titles. Condensed italic uppercase with a black text shadow so it survives sitting on a gauge.

body.purpose: Everything said to a human. Plain system UI, capped at 62ch.

label.purpose: RESET, INSTALL, macOS · Swift. Wide tracking (+0.24em to +0.3em) is what separates a label from a plate. Never used as a kicker above a headline.

mono.purpose: Commands, terminal output, demo captions, and data keys at 0.72rem. Anything a machine said first.

shadows.name: gauge-casing
shadows.purpose: The 44px gauge's chrome bevel, inside a 2.5px solid black outer border.

shadows.name: gauge-casing-compact
shadows.purpose: The 22px widget-row gauge, inside a 2px black border.

shadows.name: leading-edge-bloom
shadows.purpose: The only glow in the system. Rides the 3px near-white head of the fill. Compact variant: 3px 0 7px 0 rgba(255,246,214,.45).

shadows.name: floating-panel
shadows.purpose: The widget floating on the desktop stage. Mirrors the app's NSShadow (black 0.55, offset -3, blur 12).

shadows.name: window-drop
shadows.purpose: The terminal window on the stage. Deepest shadow in the system; it exists to say this is a real window.

shadows.name: plate-text
shadows.purpose: On every plate and numeral, matching the app's 2.5px-blur black text shadow.

motion.name: fill-ease
motion.purpose: Per-frame approach of the gauge fill toward its target. App uses 0.18.

motion.name: trail-lag
motion.purpose: Per-frame approach of the red trail. Deliberately ~3.5x slower than the fill; the gap is the effect. App uses 0.055.

motion.name: danger-pulse
motion.purpose: Fires only when the gauge is under 20 percent. App equivalent: a 10 percent white blend driven by a sine.

motion.name: panel-expand
motion.purpose: The widget unfolding from one row to three. Rows 2 and 3 fade in at .2s with .1s delay.

motion.name: round-marker
motion.purpose: The ROUND N plate over the stage on reset.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: freeze drain, pulse, and panel transition; repaint countdown on a 1s interval
motion.purpose: The whole authored moment stops under prefers-reduced-motion; the clock keeps telling the truth.

geometry.name: shear
geometry.purpose: The only shear in the system. main.swift SHEAR = 0.30 (top edge displaced by 0.30 x height); the web equivalent is skewX(-16.7deg).

geometry.name: widget-compact
geometry.purpose: The app panel at 1:1. Each extra gauge row adds 62px (ROW_PITCH).

components.name: Health Bar
components.description: The signature component: a sheared gauge with a graphite striped track, a lagging red trail, an amber-to-yellow fill, a near-white leading edge, and a chrome bevel in a black border.
components.css: .ds-bar{position:relative;height:44px;width:100%;transform:skewX(-16.7deg);transform-origin:bottom left;border:2.5px solid #000;background:repeating-linear-gradient(45deg,rgba(255,255,255,.05) 0 1.5px,transparent 1.5px 9px),linear-gradient(0deg,var(--track-lo,#101216),var(--track-hi,#272b32));box-shadow:inset 0 1.6px 0 var(--chrome-hi,#d8dee7),inset 0 0 0 2px var(--chrome-lo,#5a606b),inset 0 -6px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.55);overflow:hidden}.ds-bar>i{position:absolute;inset:0;display:block}.ds-bar-trail{background:linear-gradient(0deg,var(--trail-lo,#9e1a11),var(--trail-hi,#ff3b2f));clip-path:inset(0 calc(100% - var(--t) * 1%) 0 0)}.ds-bar-fill{background:linear-gradient(90deg,var(--health-lo,#ff8a14),var(--health-hi,#ffe968));clip-path:inset(0 calc(100% - var(--h) * 1%) 0 0)}.ds-bar-fill::after{content:"";position:absolute;left:0;right:0;top:0;height:50%;background:linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(255,255,255,.30),rgba(255,255,255,.02))}.ds-bar-fill::before{content:"";position:absolute;top:0;bottom:0;width:3px;left:calc(var(--h) * 1%);transform:translateX(-100%);background:var(--tip,#fff6d6);box-shadow:4px 0 12px 1px rgba(255,246,214,.5)}.ds-bar-notch{position:absolute;left:20%;top:0;bottom:0;width:1.5px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.22)}.ds-bar-notch::after{content:"";position:absolute;bottom:0;left:-3px;border:4px solid transparent;border-bottom-color:rgba(255,255,255,.55);border-top:0}

components.name: Health Bar (danger)
components.description: The same gauge under 20 percent: the fill swaps to alarm red to flare orange and pulses brightness. The only place red-as-fill is allowed.
components.css: .ds-bar{position:relative;height:44px;width:100%;transform:skewX(-16.7deg);transform-origin:bottom left;border:2.5px solid #000;background:repeating-linear-gradient(45deg,rgba(255,255,255,.05) 0 1.5px,transparent 1.5px 9px),linear-gradient(0deg,var(--track-lo,#101216),var(--track-hi,#272b32));box-shadow:inset 0 1.6px 0 var(--chrome-hi,#d8dee7),inset 0 0 0 2px var(--chrome-lo,#5a606b),inset 0 -6px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.55);overflow:hidden}.ds-bar>i{position:absolute;inset:0;display:block}.ds-bar-trail{background:linear-gradient(0deg,var(--trail-lo,#9e1a11),var(--trail-hi,#ff3b2f));clip-path:inset(0 calc(100% - var(--t) * 1%) 0 0)}.ds-bar-fill{background:linear-gradient(90deg,var(--health-lo,#ff8a14),var(--health-hi,#ffe968));clip-path:inset(0 calc(100% - var(--h) * 1%) 0 0)}.ds-bar-fill::before{content:"";position:absolute;top:0;bottom:0;width:3px;left:calc(var(--h) * 1%);transform:translateX(-100%);background:var(--tip,#fff6d6);box-shadow:4px 0 12px 1px rgba(255,246,214,.5)}.ds-bar-danger .ds-bar-fill{background:linear-gradient(90deg,var(--danger-lo,#e01b0c),var(--danger-hi,#ff6b3d));animation:ds-pulse 1.1s ease-in-out infinite}@keyframes ds-pulse{0%,100%{filter:brightness(1)}50%{filter:brightness(1.22)}}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-bar-danger .ds-bar-fill{animation:none}}

components.name: Plate + Key Readout
components.description: A gauge's caption line: a tracked condensed italic plate on the left, the value and the API key it came from on the right.

components.name: Countdown
components.description: The oversized reset clock. Tabular condensed italic 800 with dim seconds and a tracked RESET label beneath.

components.name: Copy Control
components.description: The system's only button. Skewed chrome-stroked ghost that inverts to a yellow fill on hover; the label is counter-skewed so it reads level.

components.name: Install Block
components.description: The primary call to action. A recessed mono well whose $ prompts are dim and unselectable, headed by a tracked label with a rule that pushes the copy control right.

narrative.overview:
ClaudeHP borrows the one interface every player reads without thinking: the fighting game health bar above the arena. The world is a matte black cabinet, and the only lit object on it is a sheared amber gauge with a chrome bevel and a red trail lagging behind the damage. Everything else in the system, body copy, terminal text, install block, is instrumentation around that gauge. The bar is not decoration on top of a product page; it is the page's first sentence.

Ground truth lives in the native app. main.swift's enum Ink and SHEAR = 0.30 define the palette and the geometry; the web tokens in site/index.html's :root were derived from them and agree value for value. Where the app and the web disagree, the app is the source of truth. One divergence stands on purpose: the app draws lettering in DINCondensed-Bold (a macOS system face, with a heavy system fallback), while the web ships Barlow Condensed 700/800 italic as a webfont because DIN Condensed is not available on the open web. Both read as the same condensed italic HUD voice; new web surfaces use Barlow Condensed.

Density is arcade, not editorial: the top band is loud and oversized, then the page drops to quiet system-UI prose at 17-19px with a 62ch measure. The system refuses the dev-tool landing grammar it was built against, headline over subtitle over screenshot card over three feature columns. Here the mechanism runs first, live, at full width, and the words arrive afterward.
keyCharacteristics: Matte black ground (#0a0b0e), no page-level gradient, no ambient glow
Sheared parallelogram gauges (shear 0.30, equal to skewX(-16.7deg)), never rounded
One amber-to-yellow light source: the gauge and its near-white leading edge
Red trail that lags the drain; red-orange pulse under 20 percent
Condensed italic uppercase plates for every label and number; system UI for prose; system mono for commands and data keys
Every number carries the key it came from (limits[kind=session])

rules.name: The One Light Source Rule
rules.body: The gauge's leading edge is the only thing in this world that glows. Every other shadow is diffuse black. No accent glow, no colored drop shadow, no neon outline anywhere else.

rules.name: The Red Means Damage Rule
rules.body: Red is never a brand color, a link, a button, or an error chrome. Red appears only where health was just lost (the trail) or is about to run out (the sub-20-percent fill). If a surface has no draining quantity, it has no red.

rules.name: The Amber Floor Rule
rules.body: Amber and yellow are confined to the gauge, the fact-row chips, and single-word emphasis. Amber never fills a card, a section band, or a page background.

rules.name: The Plate Rule
rules.body: Every HUD word is a plate: condensed, italic, uppercase, tracked, with a 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.85) shadow so it survives sitting directly on a gauge. Sentence-case condensed italic is not part of this system.

rules.name: The Receipt Rule
rules.body: A displayed number is followed by the key it came from, set in mono at 0.72rem in dim (limits[kind=session]). The claim and its source ship together or the number does not ship.

rules.name: The Voice Rule
rules.body: Copy is short and human. No dashes as connectors, no marketing formulas, no adjective stacking. Commands are the call to action; the install block is the button.

rules.name: The Bar First Rule
rules.body: Nothing renders above the health bar. No nav, no logo row, no announcement strip, no headline. The first painted object on any ClaudeHP surface is the gauge.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose never exceeds 62ch, no matter how wide the band is.

rules.name: The Bevel Not Elevation Rule
rules.body: Surfaces get depth from inset chrome strokes. Drop shadows are reserved for things that are literally floating in the depicted desktop: the widget and the terminal window. Cards, rows, and blocks stay flat on black with a hairline edge.

rules.name: The No Hard Offset Rule
rules.body: Every shadow in this world is blurred and black. Hard offset shadows belong to a neobrutalist world; this one is a machined cabinet.

rules.name: The Shear Rule
rules.body: 0.30 is the only shear in this system. Nothing is skewed at a different angle, and nothing sheared is ever given a corner radius.

rules.name: The Shared Clock Rule
rules.body: The hero gauge, the widget, and the terminal read from one state object and repaint in one frame. If a surface shows a number that also exists elsewhere on the page, it is the same number from the same tick or it does not ship.

rules.name: The One Authored Moment Rule
rules.body: This system has exactly one motion idea: the drain, with its lagging trail, its red pulse under 20 percent, and its ROUND marker on reset. Under prefers-reduced-motion the drain stops, the pulse stops, the widget's expand transition drops, and the countdown keeps ticking on a 1s interval. No scroll reveals, no parallax, no entrance animations.

dos: Do open every surface with the gauge. The bar is the first painted object, full width, before any word.
Do derive palette and geometry from main.swift (enum Ink, SHEAR = 0.30). The app is the source of truth; the web :root mirrors it.
Do pair every displayed number with its source key in dim mono (limits[kind=session]).
Do keep the trail slower than the fill (0.045 vs 0.16 web, 0.055 vs 0.18 app). The lag is the effect.
Do swap the fill to alarm-red and pulse below 20 percent, and nowhere else.
Do label simulated data plainly, in mono, next to the thing it describes (demo · numbers are simulated).
Do use the skewed chrome-stroked control as the button form, with counter-skewed label text.
Do cap prose at 62ch and set it in the plain system UI face at 17-19px.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion by freezing the drain and the widget transition while the countdown keeps ticking.
donts: Don't put a headline, nav, logo bar, or announcement strip above the health bar.
Don't round a sheared shape or shear anything at an angle other than 0.30.
Don't use red for links, buttons, brand marks, or error chrome. Red is damage.
Don't add a second light source. The leading edge glows; nothing else does.
Don't ship hard offset shadows. Shadows are blurred, black, and reserved for the widget and the terminal window.
Don't fill a card, band, or background with amber.
Don't float a tracked plate above a headline as a kicker or eyebrow. Plates label data, controls, and gauges.
Don't add a second motion idea. No scroll reveals, no parallax, no entrance animations.
Don't set condensed italic in sentence case, and don't set prose in the display face.
Don't use glyph icons or icon fonts. This system draws its own shapes (the chip, the notch, the traffic dots).
Don't mix languages in shipped copy. Web surfaces are English.
